headline: Dynamite was invented to be the safe explosive

portrait.alt: Photograph of Alfred Nobel seated sideways in a chair, bearded, his chin resting on his hand
portrait.credit: Alfred Nobel, before 1896. Gösta Florman. Public domain.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Tame the oil
slides.text: In 1864 a blast at Alfred Nobel's factory killed five people, his brother among them. **He set out to make nitroglycerin safe to handle.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: Dynamite
slides.text: Patented in 1867, dynamite was nitroglycerin soaked into porous earth, quite safe to handle. **One plant made 11 tons that year and 3,150 in 1874.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Easy to carry, for anyone
slides.text: A stable explosive can be carried into a city and left behind. **In 1885 bombers used it on the House of Commons.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Yes, in his lifetime
slides.text: Both armies used dynamite in the Franco-Prussian War, three years after the patent. **Its uses for war and terror were plain in his lifetime.**

slides.label: What came next
slides.title: Powder for armies
slides.text: Nobel went on to patent ballistite in 1887, a nearly smokeless powder Italy's army adopted. **In 1894 he bought the ironworks that became Bofors arms.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: One plant's output: 11 tons in 1867, 3,150 tons in 1874
Lucerne to Milan in about 5.5 hours instead of 27, via the Gotthard tunnel (1882)
Far less risk of accidental explosion than liquid nitroglycerin
costs: A bombing campaign in Britain, 1881 to 1885
Dynamite used by both armies in the Franco-Prussian War
Ballistite, a smokeless military powder adopted by Italy's army
slides.text: Dynamite helped build the Gotthard tunnel, cutting Lucerne to Milan from 27 hours to about 5.5. **It also put a portable bomb in anyone's hands.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: The problem moves
slides.text: Nitroglycerin's danger was going off when nobody meant it to. Dynamite fixed that, so **the risk moved to whoever held the stick.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: A fix aimed at accidents does nothing about intent. **Safe to handle also means easy to use, by anyone.**
